items.title: Narvin Kimball Interview, 1961-11-25
items.q: That's the band Pops Foster and Walter Pichon, Louis Bauerrand, that was, and I, we made the rhythm section.

ctx.x: I know he was on the boat sometime too.

He was on the boat in later years, but that, at that time, he wasn't on the boat then. Uh, he was playing locally, playing spots from different places. And, uh, I remained with him for about three months. That's the band Pops Foster and Walter Pichon, Louis Bauerrand, that was, and I, we made the rhythm section. And Eddie Cherie and, uh, Adolf Alexandria and Walter Pearson was the saxophone section.

Oh, yes. I know, I met a man on the train, Professor Lynette and I went out there two years ago, and on the way back, he was a cook on the Southern Pacific, if that's the same man. He'd once played with Celestan, he'd said, and he'd best recognize him just walking through the train. So, then he visited him. I met him, that's the first time. I never did the same since.

items.title: Narvin Kimball Interview, 1961-11-25
items.q: In fact, Pichon really instructed me. ... And Fats Pichon coached me along with that.

ctx.x: Twenty-six, I think. Twenty-eight years. Twenty-eight? Twenty-eight years and you renew it for another twenty-eight. That's fifty-six. Yeah. Well, it's about time for it to be renewed now. Yeah, the time might be coming up and be worth sharing.

Worthwhile doing. And while I was with Solid Stan's band, I did some of the arranging. We had, when he developed the larger band, we had Cecil Thornton, he was arranging. Fats Pichon did quite a bit of arranging for the band. In fact, Pichon really instructed me. I took a course from Archie Bly, a correspondence course from Archie Bly on arranging. And Fats Pichon coached me along with that. And Cecil Thornton helped me out quite a bit. And I learned to write some.
Well, I wanted to check once more on the Solid Stan band. Did you play banjo or was it bass in the Biloxi?
